newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate down, baht eases late.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate down, baht eases late.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank rate edged down on Wednesday in a market dominated by offers and thin on bidders as market liquidity remained ample, dealers said.
The increased liquidity was partly due to some selling of spot dollar/baht and forward dollar/baht positions, dealers said.
They said the overnight rate was quoted around 8.75-9.25 percent against 9.50 percent early on Wednesday.
"Even at that rate, it's hard to find borrowers," said a dealer from Thai Farmers Bank.

"Commercial banks and finance companies seemed to have money. Money from dollar/baht selling also added more liquidity. But it's too early to determine if there's any foreign inflows coming to market," he said.
The baht moved in a narrow range on Wednesday with a downward bias. It eased to 25.609/614 to the dollar late in the session from 25.596/25.607 earlier.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the baht/dollar midrate at 25.61 against 25.62 on Tuesday.
The bid/offer range of one month baht/dollar swap premium fell to 7.25-7.75 satangs per dollar from 8.00-8.50 satangs early on Wednesday.
